newsitem.title: FINLAND: Pohjola sees higher premiums in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Pohjola sees higher premiums in 1997.

text.p: Finnish insurer Pohjola said on Wednesday it expected higher premium income in 1997 but the balance on the technical account would not change markedly from 1996.
"The country's reviving economy and adjustments of the level of rates are expected to increase premiums written in 1997," Pohjola said in a statement with its 1996 results.

"The balance on the technical account is not expected to change markedly in comparison with the 1996 level from which the exceptional adjustments of technical provisions have been eliminated," it said.
Pohjola said brisk economic growth could on the other hand raise the number of claims, and operating expenses would rise because of costs relating to necessary information technology system changes.
"The development of interest rates, exchange rates and market prices will affect investment income," it said.

Pohjola's 1996 premium income was 2.57 billion markka, down from 2.58 billion in 1995, claims paid totalled 2.44 billion versus 2.27 billion and the balance on the technical account was a 437 million markka charge compared to 214 million in 1995. @
Net investment income was 962 million markka last year, up from 672 million in 1995, and the operating profit was 526 million markka, up from 461 million.
